items.q: How do I buy a strand?
items.a: Message us on WhatsApp or email with the SKU, or visit us at a show. We confirm current availability, price, selling unit and shipping before sending an invoice. Catalog photographs and historical product records do not establish current stock.
Yes, on US orders over $100. Orders under $100 ship at cost, which we confirm before you pay.

items.q: Do you sell to shops and designers at wholesale?
items.a: Yes. Most of our regular buyers are designers and bead shops. Tell us what you make and how often you buy and we will set you up with a reorder list.

items.q: Can I reserve strands and pick them up at a show?
items.a: Yes. Send the SKUs a few days before the show and we bring them to the booth. Unpaid reservations are held for the first day only.
We ship worldwide from Cupertino, California. Customs duties and taxes at the destination are the buyer's responsibility, and delivery times vary by country.
Unaltered strands can be returned within 30 days. Strands that have been cut, restrung or worn cannot be returned. Natural color and size variation within the stated range is not a defect.
Each listing identifies the material, shape, size and cut from our product records. Ask us to confirm the specific strand, material and any treatment details before ordering.

items.q: What is the difference between precious and semi-precious?
items.a: Precious is the traditional label for ruby, sapphire and emerald. Semi-precious covers everything else, including some of the rarest stones we stock. We use both labels because buyers search by them, not because one shelf is better than the other.
Measurements are recorded in millimeters. An x separates dimensions, such as width and length; a hyphen indicates a range of sizes. Ask us to confirm the actual strand's measurements before ordering.
Strand lengths are shown where recorded in our product details. Confirm the exact strand length and selling unit before ordering.

items.q: How should I care for gemstone beads?
items.a: Store strands separately so harder stones do not scratch softer ones, keep them away from perfume and household chemicals, and clean with a soft dry cloth. Opal, pearl, fluorite, rhodochrosite and larimar are soft or porous and need the most care; sapphire, spinel and garnet are hard enough for daily wear.

Kunzite, amethyst and some topaz can fade with long sun exposure. Hydrophane Ethiopian opal changes temporarily when it absorbs water. Ask us for care guidance for the specific material you are considering.
